discovery: Prediction and discovery of kilonovae, establishing neutron-star mergers as a cosmic site of r-process heavy-element production

nominees.name: Daniel Kasen
nominees.affiliation: University of California, Berkeley and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, USA

motivation: The origin of the heavy elements such as gold and uranium was one of the oldest open problems in physics. Metzger and collaborators (2010) worked out from first principles how radioactive decay of freshly made r-process nuclei in neutron-star merger ejecta powers a transient, which they called a kilonova. Kasen then showed that lanthanide opacities make these transients red and infrared, which told observers where to look. Tanvir led the first detection of a kilonova, following GRB 130603B (2013). The spectacular kilonova that accompanied GW170817 in 2017 confirmed the picture, with in situ evidence of r-process material. Taken together, this work turned speculation into measurement. It links nuclear physics, gravitational waves and the chemical fingerprints we find in the oldest stars and in dwarf galaxies such as Reticulum II. It is a textbook example of theory predicting a new phenomenon that observation then confirmed.
